messages:
maya.chen: Hey — running into flaky SSL failures from the Python SDK on Windows 10 with CPython 3.8. Error is: 

ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate

This is from our internal staging endpoint (private cert chain). Works fine on macOS and linux runners. Anyone seen this on Windows + py3.8/3.9?

sam.gupta: Do you have the full traceback? Are you using system Python, or Anaconda? Also what does `pip show certifi` say? Windows historically needs certifi or python-certifi-win32 to bridge the Windows CA store.

maya.chen: Traceback pasted below (trimmed): 

requests.exceptions.SSLError: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='api.staging.redwood', port=443): Max retries exceeded with url: /v1/ (Caused by SSLError(SSLCertVerificationError("[SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:1123)")))

`pip show certifi` -> Name: certifi
Version: 2023.11.XX
Location: C:\Users\maya\envs\rwd\Lib\site-packages

Using venv, installed with pip (not conda).

alex.kim: Two things we've observed: (1) Our Windows wheels historically weren't published for older py versions so users fall back to sdist -> build which can end up using the system OpenSSL; some Windows Pythons ship without a bundled cert store. (2) Some enterprise proxies replace certs. Quick try: `pip install python-certifi-win32` and restart Python — that makes `certifi.where()` point into a cert bundle that mirrors Windows store.

sam.gupta: Also try forcing the SDK to use certifi bundle directly as a diagnostic: 

```
# quick debug to check what SSL context is used
python -c "import ssl, certifi; print('certifi:', certifi.where()); print(ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where()))"
```

If that works, we can improve SDK to explicitly use certifi when requests is used.

maya.chen: Tried python-certifi-win32 — still failing. The debug prints show certifi path OK, but requests still fails when hitting our staging host. The TLS handshake logs show chain building fails at one intermediary (internal CA). Works on linux CI (self-hosted) and mac windows on another laptop.

patrick: Could be that our staging cert chain omits a cross-signed intermediate that some OpenSSL builds don't auto-fetch. Windows + older OpenSSL versions don't do AIA fetching. Short-term: add an env var to SDK to allow passing CA bundle path (e.g., REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE) so ops can point to the full chain. Long-term: vendor certifi or ship a bundled CA file in the wheel for Windows.

alex.kim: Agreed. Also file: we currently only run SDK tests on ubuntu-latest in GH actions. We should add matrix entries for windows-latest with py3.8 and py3.11 and run a small TLS smoke test against our public staging cert (or a recorded cassette) to catch regressions.

maya.chen: That env var workaround is fine for now. Which API in the SDK accepts custom bundle? I couldn't find it in 0.9.2 docs.

sam.gupta: Good catch — SDK doesn't expose CA bundle config right now. It accepts `timeout`, `max_retries`, `api_key`, but not `ca_bundle` or `verify`. We should add support for a `verify` param (bool or str path) that maps to requests.Session.verify. Also accept REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE env var. Patch is straightforward.

patrick: I'll create a tiny issue and assign to eng-infra/devex. Action items: 
- Add REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE and SDK config `verify` param (patrick)
- Publish guidance in DevEx docs for Windows troubleshooting (sam)
- Add GH Actions windows-latest py3.8/3.11 jobs and TLS smoke test (alex)
- Consider vendoring certifi or including it as required dependency for Windows wheels (engineering follow-up)

ci-bot: Issue created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python-sdk/issues/482 — "Windows + py3.8: SSL cert verification failures + CA bundle option" assigned to @patrick, labels: bug, platform-windows

maya.chen: Thanks everyone. I'll use the REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE workaround for the staging deploy and paste the exact steps here once validated. One more ask — any plan to keep supporting 3.8? Our infra still has a handful of 3.8 instances. Customers also ask about 3.8 compatibility.

alex.kim: We plan to support 3.8—3.12 for the next year but we need CI coverage matrix and binary wheels for Windows for each supported Python. If we add windows wheels it will reduce these kinds of issues. Also: we should add typing stubs for the async client and run mypy in CI; typing gaps make it hard for users writing async code on Windows.

sam.gupta: Feature request noted: async client parity on Windows + typing. Please add separate GH issue for typing/async tests.

patrick: Summary (short): implement `verify` config + REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE; add windows CI; publish doc; follow-up on wheels/typing. I'll assign owners.

maya.chen: Confirmed workaround works if I point REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE to the full-bundle.pem file (contains intermediate + root). Staging now passes. Will paste repro steps in the issue. :white_check_mark:

sam.gupta: Nice — thanks for confirming. We'll aim to get the SDK patch in the next patch release.

maya.chen: cc @support — heads-up in case customers hit this on Windows.

patrick: tagging this for release notes: windows-py-compat fixes and new config var.

alex.kim: Also adding a small sample app in examples/windows that demonstrates setting REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE and an async example using `async with RedwoodAsyncClient(...)` (once types are in).

maya.chen: Great. Appreciate the fast follow-up.
